title: shadow-ops cornersheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick scribbles for the night shadow shift — lightweight checklist + ephemeral procedures you can use while the main runbook is out for edits. Treat this as a pocket cheat-sheet: authoritative only until PR lands.

Context notes:
- Service: redwood-serving (model runtime cluster) + api-gateway.
- Common mode: degraded latency during KGW spikes or cold-KV storms.
- Recent history: rolling kernel update last week, minor cache-evict bug suspected.

Immediate triage checklist (fast):
1) Check PagerDuty alert -> severity tag. If P1 escalate immediately to oncall-sre and ENG-SERVING.
2) Console: Console > Routes > last 15m tokens per route. Look for sudden token spike.
3) SLOs: confirm 95p latency in the Console. If >2x target, add "latency" label in incident.
4) Check routing fallbacks: run `curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://console.local/api/v1/routes/active` and spot routes using fallback-model.

Quick commands (one-liners):
- tail recent pod logs: `kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime --tail=200`
- search for cache errors: `kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime | grep -i "kv cache" -n`
- restart a bad worker (if CPU stuck >90%): `kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime-worker`

Temporary mitigations (safe, reversible):
- Route low-priority traffic to dedicated-burst pool: set route override in Console (notes: this increases cost; notify finance if left >4h).
- Reduce batch_size on route to 1 for offending path to reduce tail latency (Console -> route config -> advanced -> batching override).
- Enable model-variant fallback to quantized if OOMs observed (Console -> model catalog -> variant: quantized-v1).

Known weirds and checks:
- 'kv cache priming' can cause short CPU spikes during first heavy request window; check pod "priming" logs and let them warm for 5-10m.
- Intermittent 502s from api-gateway often correlate with stale TLS cert rotation on dedicated nodes; check node cert expiry at /infra/certs.

Escalation ladder (fast):
- On-call SRE -> Slack @oncall-sre -> if no response in 10m, call line: +1-555-0132 (ops pager).
- Pager to Eng Serving Runtime (if model runtime suspected) -> mention dedicated pool id and recent rollout hash.

Notes-to-self / TODOs for morning handover:
- File a follow-up in JIRA with logs tarball link and suspected commit hash.
- If KV cache priming appears >20% of p95 tokens, schedule a small canary to pre-warm caches at low-traffic hours.
- Update primary runbook with the safe-bounce threshold (currently 90% CPU and 10m sustained).

Temporary scripts & snippets (place here for quick copy):
- Gather quick diag bundle: `kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide > /tmp/pods.txt && kubectl -n redwood describe pods > /tmp/pods.desc && tar czf /tmp/diag-$(date +%s).tgz /tmp/pods.*`
- Get recent heavy routes: `curl -sS https://console.local/api/v1/metrics/routes?window=15m | jq '.routes | sort_by(.p95) | reverse | .[:10] '`

Open questions / confusions to pass on:
- Did the kernel update include the new memcpy micro-optimizations on the serving nodes? If yes, correlate to any memory accounting changes.
- Who owns the dedicated-burst pool billing alarm? (Tag: finance-alerts?)

Sign-off template for handover message: (paste into Slack)
> quick handover: shadow shift observed spikes at HH:MM. Applied batching override on route X -> reduced p95 by ~30% in 10m. Will file JIRA-RI-4821 with logs. Next shift please monitor KV cache priming and keep dedicated-burst routing enabled until 09:30 PT.

Random notes / shorthand (for me):
- fallback-model = quantized-v1
- burst-pool-id = db-pool-03
- last-rollout = 2025-02-27-4a1b

If you add anything here, mark with initials and date. Keep it short.

Maya C. 2025-03-03
